Build a state panel

Source: R/build_states_panel.R
build_states_panel.Rd

Build a state panel

Usage

build_states_panel(
  start_year = 1946,
  end_year = 2013,
  coding_system = c("cow", "gw"),
  exclude_microstates = TRUE,
  exclude_non_un = TRUE,
  exclude_islands = FALSE,
  unit = c("year", "quarter", "month", "day")
)

Arguments

start_year

First year. Must be 1816 or later.

end_year

Last year. Must be 2025 or earlier.

coding_system

Country coding system. Either "cow" or "gw".

exclude_microstates

Logical. Exclude entities identified as microstates by states::state_panel().

exclude_non_un

Logical. Exclude the package's fixed set of non-UN entities (Kosovo, Taiwan, Hong Kong, the European Union, and South Vietnam for COW; Kosovo, Abkhazia, South Ossetia, Taiwan, and South Vietnam for GW).

exclude_islands

Logical. Exclude six small Caribbean island states: Dominica, Grenada, Saint Lucia, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Antigua and Barbuda, and Saint Kitts and Nevis.

unit

Time unit of the panel: "year" (default), "quarter", "month", or "day". A state is included in a period if it was a member of the state system for any part of that period.

Value

A data frame with one row per state and period. A country-year panel has the country code, year, and country; a country-quarter panel adds quarter (1-4); a country-month panel adds month (1-12); a country-day panel adds month, day, and date.

Details

Annual data (add_gdp(), add_population(), add_military_expenditure(), add_vdem()) are joined to a country-quarter, country-month, or country-day panel by country and year, so every period of a year takes that year's value. add_leader_data() uses the leaders' exact dates in office, and add_conflict() aggregates event data to the panel's own unit, for the datasets that record exact event dates. add_lag() and add_spell_duration() count periods in the panel's unit. Use aggregate_panel() to collapse a finer panel to a coarser unit.

A country-day panel is large (about 70,000 rows per year of data), so restrict it to the years you need.

Examples

yearly  <- build_states_panel(1990, 2000, coding_system = "cow")
quarterly <- build_states_panel(2010, 2012, coding_system = "cow", unit = "quarter")
monthly <- build_states_panel(2010, 2012, coding_system = "gw", unit = "month")
daily   <- build_states_panel(2011, 2011, coding_system = "cow", unit = "day")
